title: Pulse cadence mini-OKR lab — weekly scratch
content:
Purpose and context:
- Quick mutable scratchpad for one-person OKR experiments. Not polished — intentionally rough. Use for weekly check-ins, tiny bets, and deciding which micro-habits to keep.

Overall northstar (micro):
- Increase meaningful deep-work hours from baseline ~6 hrs/week to 12 hrs/week by end of quarter while keeping output quality (PR reviews merged per week) stable or up.

Current baseline (week of 2025-02-03):
- Deep-work sessions (>=45m with no context switches): 3 sessions, ~4.2 hours total
- PRs merged (assigned owner): 6
- Interruptions (scheduled meetings + ad-hoc pings): 18
- Focus score (self-rated 1–5 each day): 3.1 average

Hypotheses to test this fortnight:
1) Blocked mornings (9:00–11:30) for deep work on Mondays/Wednesdays/Fridays will double session frequency with minimal meeting spillover.
   - Metric: number of >=45m sessions captured by FocusTimer per week (target +3)
   - Acceptance: see net +2 sessions/week and no drop in merged PRs
2) Replace one all-hands meeting with async update + 30m office hours will reduce interruptions by 20%.
   - Metric: # ad-hoc Slack pings in deep-work hours, measured by Slack export tags
3) Micro-planning 10 minutes at day-start reduces wasted context switches during afternoon by 15%.
   - Metric: subjective afternoon focus score, baseline 2.8 -> target 3.4

Experiment plan (this week -> next week):
- Mon/Wed/Fri: 9:00–11:30 blocked on calendar (mark as DO NOT SCHEDULE, notify team).
- Tue: 30m async-runbook + 30m office hours (replace recurring all-hands this week).
- Daily: 10m morning micro-plan (capture top-3 outcomes, 1 blocker).
- Track: use FocusTimer + short end-of-day note (1 line on progress and one ask).

Measurement sources and low-fi instrumentation:
- FocusTimer app export (CSV) for session count/duration.
- Slack: manual count for pings during blocked hours (quick daily tally).
- GitHub: PR merged count by author weekly.
- Personal end-of-day note stored in ~/notes/weekly-digest (manual aggregation).

Weekly check-in template (to use each Friday):
- Wins (3):
  1.
  2.
  3.
- Misses / noise:
  - What ate time unexpectedly?
- Data snapshot:
  - Deep sessions: X (hrs) | PRs merged: Y | Interruptions: Z
- Hypothesis status: validated / partially / invalidated
- Next steps (concrete):
  - Keep / tweak / abandon experiment?
  - If keep: document permanent calendar policy and notify 

Retrospective notes (end of last fortnight):
- What worked:
  - Blocking mornings reduced quick meetings (fewer on-calendar churn) and felt calmer.
  - Micro-planning helped triage afternoons; saved ~10 minutes each day.
- What didn't:
  - Office hours day created more async work the next day (ask backlog increased).
  - One unplanned customer sync slipped into deep-work window twice (need escalation guidelines).

Decisions and action items:
- Keep morning blocks for another 2 weeks but reduce Tue block to 9:00–10:30 to accommodate cross-team sync once. (Action: update calendar + note to team) — due 2025-02-07.
- Formalize "urgent" escalation: messages marked with prefix "URGENT-DW" can be pinged; otherwise defer. (Action: post brief Slack guideline) — due 2025-02-09.
- If PR throughput drops by >20% for 2 consecutive weeks, pause the experiment and analyze root causes. (Action: manual audit) — owner: Emma.

Open questions / unresolved:
- How to quantify quality vs quantity of PRs in a low-effort way? Could sample 2 PRs/week for a lightweight reviewer rubric.
- Is there tooling to auto-capture "deep-work" pings in Slack metadata? Might ask Eng Tools. Linked artifact: JIRA-ENG-1128.

Notes to self (quick):
- Resist optimizing focus at cost of team visibility — one-person experiments must communicate tradeoffs early.
- When productivity increases, document the exact calendar policies so others can try safely.

Quick links / references:
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-3452 (personal OKR scaffolding)
- Slack thread where I announced the experiment: https://slack-redwood-internal.example.com/threads/C12ABC34
- Jira ticket for tooling ask: JIRA-ENG-1128

Mini retros next steps (for next Friday):
- Run 2-sample PR quality rubric; add one sentence to weekly digest summarizing quality.
- Re-evaluate office hours cadence (do we keep weekly or move to every-other-week?).
- If morning blocks show +4 hrs/week deep work sustained -> propose team trial for paired mornings.

End-of-file quick log (timestamps):
- 2025-02-03 09:05 started week with morning block, 1 interrupted meeting (20m) slipped in.
- 2025-02-04 09:00 successful 2-hour uninterrupted block, felt high leverage.
- 2025-02-05 16:30 note: too many async requests piled after office hours day (adjust next week).

(End of scratchpad)
